prompt: Which standard of the family can an organisation be certified against?

choices.text: ISO/IEC 27005
choices.why: 27005 is guidance on risk management.

choices.text: ISO/IEC 27001
choices.why: Right. It states what an organisation shall do.

choices.text: ISO/IEC 27002
choices.why: 27002 is guidance; nobody is certified against it.

choices.text: ISO/IEC 27000
choices.why: 27000 is the vocabulary.

prompt: Match each standard to what it is.

pairs.right: guidance on information security risk management

prompt: A supplier sends its ISO 27001 certificate. What does the lesson say to read first?

choices.text: The list of all 93 controls
choices.why: That is in the SoA, not the certificate.

choices.text: The number of employees
choices.why: Size is not what the certificate certifies.

choices.text: The logo of the certification body
choices.why: Logos prove nothing.

choices.text: The scope
choices.why: Right. It may cover only part of the company.

prompt: An old policy cites control A.9.2.6. What does that tell you?

choices.text: It refers to 27701's privacy controls
choices.why: It is an Annex A number from 2013.

choices.text: It was written against the 2013 edition
choices.why: Right. That number does not exist in 2022.

choices.text: The policy follows the current 2022 edition
choices.why: 2022 numbers controls 5.x to 8.x.

choices.text: The control is excluded from the SoA
choices.why: The number says nothing about applicability.

prompt: Match each clause of 27001 to its subject.

choices.text: A security product that monitors the network
choices.why: It is a way of managing, not a product.

choices.text: The list of 93 controls in Annex A
choices.why: The controls are part of it; the system is the management around them.

choices.text: A certificate issued by Inmetro
choices.why: Certification bodies issue certificates; Cgcre accredits them.

choices.text: How it decides, does, checks and improves
choices.why: Right. Policies, roles, processes and records.

prompt: Under clause 6, why does the shop choose its controls?

choices.text: Because they are the cheapest available
choices.why: Cost is weighed against risk, not alone.

choices.text: Because the certification body picks them
choices.why: The body audits the choice; it does not make it.

choices.text: Its risk assessment says it needs them
choices.why: Right. The risk register is the heart of it.

choices.text: Because they appear in Annex A
choices.why: Annex A is a list to check against, not a reason.

prompt: The current text of 27001 no longer names plan, do, check, act. What does the lesson say about the cycle?
hint: Read the clauses top to bottom.

choices.text: It was replaced by the five NIST functions
choices.why: Those appear as 27002 attributes, not as the clause structure.

choices.text: It is still how the clauses fit together
choices.why: Right. Plan, do, check, improve, and around again.

choices.text: It now applies only to Annex A
choices.why: The cycle concerns the management system.

choices.text: It was removed, so the clauses are independent
choices.why: The clauses still form the cycle.

prompt: How many controls does Annex A of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 hold?
Match each theme of Annex A to its number of controls.
Lesson 12's backups correspond to which Annex A control?

choices.text: 8.13 information backup
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: 8.22 segregation of networks
choices.why: That is lesson 5.

choices.text: 5.15 access control
choices.why: That is lesson 6.

choices.text: 5.3 segregation of duties
choices.why: That is lesson 6's separation of duties.

prompt: What does it say that 37 of the 93 controls are organisational and 34 technological?

choices.text: Organisational controls are easier to implement
choices.why: Nothing says they are easier.

choices.text: Much of what is audited is decisions and processes
choices.why: Right. Not configuration alone.

choices.text: Technology does not matter for certification
choices.why: 34 controls are technological.

choices.text: The standard was written for large companies only
choices.why: Its size is not about company size.

prompt: What does the statement of applicability record for each Annex A control?

choices.text: Whether it applies, why, and its status
choices.why: Right. Plus where the evidence is.

choices.text: The price of each control
choices.why: Cost is not a column.

choices.text: Which employee installed it
choices.why: Ownership lives elsewhere.

choices.text: Only the controls that are fully implemented
choices.why: It covers all 93, implemented or not.

prompt: Which justification for excluding a control would an auditor accept?
hint: Does the activity exist in scope?

choices.text: No software is developed in scope
choices.why: Right. The activity does not exist in scope.

choices.text: The previous auditor did not ask about it
choices.why: That says nothing about applicability.

choices.text: It is too expensive this year
choices.why: Cost goes in the risk decision, not an exclusion.

choices.text: We have never done it
choices.why: Not having done it is not a reason it does not apply.

prompt: The shop's risk assessment needs a control that is not in Annex A. What does 27001 expect?
hint: Annex A is not a ceiling.

choices.text: Ask ISO to add it to the next edition first
choices.why: No need to wait for a new edition.

choices.text: Replace an Annex A control with it
choices.why: Nothing has to be removed to add one.

choices.text: Leave the risk untreated, since only Annex A controls count
choices.why: Any control the risks need counts.

choices.text: Add the control and include it in the SoA
choices.why: Right. The controls come from the risks.

prompt: Order the steps of the certification cycle.
items: stage 2: does the ISMS actually run?
surveillance audit in the first year
surveillance audit in the second year
trap: A certificate is issued after stage 2 and kept by the yearly visits.

prompt: For how many years is an ISO 27001 certificate valid?
What does the lesson advise a nine-person shop about ISO 27001?

choices.text: Certify at once, whatever it costs
choices.why: Certify when somebody needs the certificate.

choices.text: Use it now; certify when needed
choices.why: Right. With a scope no larger than that customer needs.

choices.text: Ignore it, since it is for large companies
choices.why: The clauses and Annex A are useful at any size.

choices.text: Certify only the physical controls first
choices.why: Certification covers the ISMS for a scope, not one theme.

prompt: What should you check on a supplier's ISO 27001 certificate? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: that the supplier has no excluded controls in its SoA
choices.why: Justified exclusions are normal.

choices.text: that the certification body is accredited
choices.why: Third.

choices.text: that it is current and against the 2022 edition
choices.why: Second.

choices.text: that the scope covers the service you buy
choices.why: First.
